transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-12-20 16:00 PST — Duration: 62 mins — Attendees: Liam (Redwood AE), Marisol (Redwood SE), Devon (Redwood SE), Sanjay (Galileo CTO), Maya (ML Eng), Renee (Platform), Tomás (SRE)

Summary (auto): quick intro, then dive into cost modeling and bench plan. Lots of detail on batching and cache. End with clear next steps and owners.

[00:00] Liam (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — quick intros, we're going to focus on the pilot scope and the unit econ questions you sent over.
[00:18] Sanjay (Galileo): Yeah thanks, Liam — we are under a pretty tight budget runway so this is kinda the priority — we need to know per-1k-token costs and what we can tune to hit 1 month of inference budget.
[00:30] Marisol (Redwood SE): Cool. To be explicit, we'll run a 2-week dedicated benchmark on a reserved pool, and measure throughput/latency and per-token cost with different batching and cache configs. We'll include a quantized model variant too.
[00:47] Maya (Galileo): When you say "per-token cost" — is that raw infra cost or Redwood list price? We need both to model our unit econ.
[00:56] Liam: We'll provide both: infra-equivalent cost estimates (what a self-hosted team would pay) and Redwood hosted/dedicated pricing examples so you can see margin.
[01:06] Tomás (Galileo): Our big ask is tail latency — p95 under 350ms for ~256 token completions, ideally 95th <300ms; p50 is nicer but less critical. That affects how much batching we can tolerate.
[01:22] Devon (Redwood SE): Right, batching lowers cost per token but increases latency. We'll show a curve: cost per 1k tokens vs p95 latency at different batch windows. Also show prefix/KV cache impact — if you have repeated system prompts or long context we can cache KV layers to speed up next-token calls.
[01:40] Sanjay: Explain KV cache again — in our app we do lots of short-turn chats then longer summarizations. Will caching help?
[01:49] Marisol: Yes — prefix caching reduces recompute for repeated prefixes. For chat-heavy workloads, caching can drop per-token cost by ~15-40% depending on hit rate. We'll test candidate hit rates 20%, 50%, 80% in the harness.
[02:05] Maya: And quantization? We have concerns about quality degradation.
[02:09] Marisol: We'll include a quantized 4-bit run as an option; we'll run quality checks against your eval prompts. If quality drop is within your regression threshold (we'll use your acceptance tests), it's likely worth the cost savings.
[02:20] Sanjay: What's a typical per-1k token delta with batching + cache + quant? ballpark.
[02:24] Liam: Ballpark: hosted API baseline maybe $0.045 per 1k tokens on large-arch models; with dedicated infra and aggressive batching + cache + q4 it can go below $0.01 per 1k tokens for high-throughput NLP workloads. But depends heavily on sequence length and hit rates. We'll give a modeled spreadsheet with scenarios.
[02:44] Renee (Galileo): Our compliance team requires SOC2, ISO and a KMS flow for key management — can you provide redwood's package?
[02:52] Liam: Yes — we'll attach our security pack. For private/VPC we'll open a ticket with our security team to walk you through.
[03:00] Sanjay: Network egress costs? If you run dedicated in our cloud account, do we pay egress?
[03:06] Devon: If it's in your VPC, infra egress follows your cloud terms; for hosted, we include typical egress in pricing examples. We'll annotate our spreadsheet with network assumptions.
[03:20] Maya: For the benchmark harness — we want 3 workloads: 1) short chat (avg 40 tokens), 2) mid-form Q&A (avg 220 tokens), 3) long summarization (avg 1,100 tokens).
[03:33] Marisol: Perfect. We'll parameterize the harness for traffic patterns: steady-sustained vs spiky bursts, and test with live-like concurrency profiles.
[03:45] Sanjay: Timeline? We need numbers before end of Q1 runway decision (early Feb).
[03:51] Liam: Proposed: you deliver traces by 12/28, we spin up a dedicated trial early Jan (requested start 01/04), run 2-week bench, results review 01/18, contract/commit discussions by end of Jan. That's aggressive but doable.
[04:10] Tomás: Any chance we can do 1-week dry run earlier? smaller scale?
[04:13] Marisol: Yes, we can do a 3-4 day warmup in your account to validate harness and configs. We'll include that in the plan.
[04:25] Sanjay: Ok good. On the cost modeling side, we want a dashboard-style output: expected cost per 1M tokens under different knob settings, and sensitivity to avg seq len and cache hit.
[04:36] Liam: We'll provide a sheet with scenario tabs: baseline hosted, dedicated conservative, dedicated aggressive, and a sensitivity tab. We'll include break-even points for reserve vs on-demand.
[04:48] Maya: About batching knobs — what's configurable? latency budget vs batch size?
[04:53] Devon: We expose target latency (SLO), max batch size, micro-batching window, and auto-batching policies. For example, you can set target p95 <= 300ms and we auto-limit batch size or fall back to a faster model variant.
[05:10] Marisol: Also important: routing policies — route to cheaper region or smaller model if a request isn't latency critical. We'll show routing config examples.
[05:20] Sanjay: If we see quality regressions on q4 quant, is rollback immediate?
[05:24] Liam: We have rollout policies — canary + automatic fallback. If eval metrics drop below threshold, traffic shifts back to baseline. We'll include runbooks in the doc.
[05:36] Renee: Who's responsible for the harness instrumentation? We need Prom metrics into our Grafana.
[05:40] Marisol: We'll provide exporters and tracing hooks; we can push Prom style metrics and sample dashboards. We'll add that to the deliverables.
[05:52] Sanjay: Pricing curiosity — reserved capacity commitments — is there a minimum term?
[05:56] Liam: Standard is monthly or annual. For pilot we can do a trial reserved pool for 2 weeks as a gesture; committed pricing starts with 1-month min in most cases but we can be flexible for pilots.
[06:08] Maya: Any constraints with our infra — we're GCP us-west2 primarily.
[06:12] Devon: We support GCP regions; we'll note region-specific perf in the benchmark. If necessary we can run in multi-region to test failover.
[06:25] Sanjay: Okay let's recap immediate asks...
[06:28] Liam: Recap: Redwood sends cost model spreadsheet + security pack + benchmark harness link. Customer provides workload traces and eval prompts by 12/28. Pilot kickoff targeted 01/04 with a 2-week run and results review 01/18.
[06:41] Marisol: Action owners in the doc — we'll set up the shared folder now, you'll get invites.
[06:46] Tomás: Fine — one more question: are there hard limits on batch size when KV cache enabled?
[06:50] Marisol: Practically, cache doesn't limit batch size but it changes the compute mix — many tokens served from cache are cheaper. We'll measure both.
[06:58] Sanjay: Great. Thanks team, look forward to the spreadsheet.
[07:02] Liam: Thanks all, we'll follow up and send invites. Bye.

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-hearings on acronyms (e.g., K-V cache typed as "K V cash"), speaker overlap near the end.

Attachments/links referenced: cost-model-sheet (link to drive), benchmark-harness repo (link), redwood-security-pack.pdf (link).
notes: Representative success criteria captured: p95 < 300-350ms for 256 token completions (customer target), cost scenarios under conservative/aggressive batching+cache+q4. Pilot plan: 2-week dedicated benchmark starting 2027-01-04, with 3 workload types (short, mid, long).
